name: Trusted FOOD-001 exact-read dependency composition for private menu runtime
phase: Discovery and specification only; implementation requires separate authorization
purpose: Provide an explicit frozen two-method infrastructure projection of an already-injected FOOD-001 repository for menu exact-reference verification, without changing private services or selecting production storage.

currentContracts.dependencyType: export type FoodMenuReadDependencies = Pick<FoodDraftRepository, 'getProduct' | 'getRecipe'>; defined in ./menu-persistence
currentContracts.readResult: FoodDraftReadResult<T> = Readonly<{ outcome: 'found'; snapshot: T } | { outcome: 'not-found' }>; no null and no ok/value/error wrapper
currentContracts.repository: Both methods are on the same FoodDraftRepository interface and are implemented by InMemoryFoodDraftRepository and D1FoodDraftRepository. They validate canonical identity and positive safe-integer version, query exact coordinates, and never substitute latest or mutate records. Invalid coordinates throw/reject FoodDraftValidationError; storage/decoding failures throw/reject FoodDraftStorageError. Successful snapshots are detached and recursively frozen by FOOD-001 validation/deserialization.
currentContracts.productInternalReads: One getProduct delegation may cause the FOOD-001 repository to read its recorded exact recipe for decoding/validation. Q promises one intended repository-method invocation, not one SQL query or zero nested recipe reads. This inherited behavior must remain intact.
currentContracts.serviceMismatch: FoodPrivateDraftService maps each repository operation to Promise<FoodDraftServiceResult<rawResult>>, where FoodDraftServiceResult is ok:true/value or ok:false/error with five service codes. It freshly authorizes first and sanitizes repository failures as invalid-input/storage. It preserves exact versions but is neither statically nor semantically the raw dependency contract. The mismatch includes access decisions and failure channels, not merely an object wrapper.
currentContracts.constructors: D1FoodDraftRepository(database: FoodD1Database) is already an injected synchronous constructor and performs no I/O at construction. No additional repository factory or persistence implementation is needed. FoodD1Database exposes prepare and batch; Q neither accepts nor acquires it.
currentContracts.runtimeExposure: FOOD-001E/F/G expose authorized service results, and K adds service/gate from the same service instance. They deliberately hide repositories. Q must not reach into those objects or widen their surfaces.

consumerEvidence.callSites: Both InMemoryFoodMenuRepository and D1FoodMenuRepository capture/bind getProduct/getRecipe in their constructors. Their #draftContext calls getProduct(exact product ID/version) then getRecipe(exact recipe ID/version); throws/rejections map to menu storage. Presentation validation calls #draftContext; offer/publication/availability validation transitively traverses exact presentations. No other direct calls to the two dependency methods occur in these adapters.
consumerEvidence.found: Consumers verify envelope shape, domain validity, returned identity/version, evidence bindings and product-to-recipe correspondence. A valid found result supplies context; malformed/corrupt or metadata-disagreeing data maps to storage. They reconstruct validated snapshots rather than granting sale authority.
consumerEvidence.missing: Missing dependency for a proposed new presentation is invalid-input. Missing dependency while verifying existing stored history is storage. This distinction belongs to the existing menu repository and must not be changed by Q.
consumerEvidence.mismatch: A structurally valid product referencing another recipe than the proposed context yields invalid-input for new content and storage for stored content. Returned coordinate disagreement or invalid domain snapshots yields storage.
consumerEvidence.tests: menu-persistence.test.ts proves exact dependency coordinates, missing/new versus missing/stored classification, thrown storage and corrupt data handling. draft-persistence.test.ts proves historical product-to-recipe versions and detached frozen reads; d1-draft-persistence.test.ts proves exact metadata/canonical payload failure handling with fake D1. Runtime tests verify injected references and method receivers. This discovery inspects tests; it does not execute a database or claim new runtime verification.

authorizationAndTrust.conclusion: These are infrastructure validation reads owned by the repository contract, not independent user-facing FOOD-001 private-service operations. FOOD-002D/G explicitly contain no authorization; FOOD-002E freshly authorizes before repository invocation. Requiring user resolution inside each referential read would couple persistence to request authorization and reinterpret existing storage failure channels. Q introduces no such authorization.
authorizationAndTrust.boundary: Q is an exported server-library infrastructure composition helper, usable only by trusted internal composition. Possession of a food ID is never permission. The capability itself is privileged because it can read private snapshots: do not expose it to routes as an alternate user API, clients, public runtime bundles or request payloads. User operations continue through the private menu service/gate and authorized FOOD-001 service unchanged.
authorizationAndTrust.structuralTrust: Structural checks cannot prove provenance or permissions. Trusted callers must supply a real approved repository capability; Q accepts no principals/roles/tokens/auth booleans and performs no identity lookup. No reusable authorization decision is issued or cached.
authorizationAndTrust.evidence: This conclusion follows the existing repository no-access-decision comments, raw Pick contract and service-before-repository authorization. It does not authorize deploying an unguarded repository API or bypassing an existing private-service method.

architectureComparison.A: Selected: project an already-injected raw repository's exact methods using the existing FoodMenuReadDependencies type.
architectureComparison.B: Do not add a duplicate exact-read interface: FoodMenuReadDependencies already expresses exactly the required capability and static signatures.
architectureComparison.C: Do not widen FOOD-001K service/gate bundles; raw infrastructure reads and user authorization capabilities have different purposes. A trusted later composition may share a known repository instance without changing K now.
architectureComparison.D: Selected only as a small pure projection wrapper, not a new repository or database adapter. It constructs no persistence or runtime graph.
architectureComparison.E: Reject service casts, private-field access and guessed envelope/error unwrapping. Using the authorized service would introduce extra access/failure semantics not present in the dependency contract.
architectureComparison.F: Existing direct bound-method wiring is already possible and tested. Q adds only a named reviewed frozen projection seam to constrain exposure and preserve receivers; it does not claim a missing storage abstraction or build another domain model.

selectedArchitecture.inputDefinition: export interface FoodMenuReadDependenciesCompositionInput { readonly repository: FoodMenuReadDependencies; }
selectedArchitecture.typeReuse: Import FoodMenuReadDependencies as a type from ./menu-persistence. Accept the already-narrow structural input; an actual FoodDraftRepository satisfies it without a cast. Do not create a second read-result type, service type or interface alias.
selectedArchitecture.output: Object.freeze({ getProduct, getRecipe }) only. No repository/database/environment/service/mutation/list/history/latest/auth capability or additional properties exposed. Do not freeze or mutate caller-owned repository or its results.
selectedArchitecture.configurationFailure: Invalid construction throws TypeError with exactly Food menu exact-read dependency configuration is unavailable. This is a synchronous construction exception, not a new repository/service/result error vocabulary.

construction.checks: Require non-null/non-array object input and repository, callable getProduct and callable getRecipe. Capture input.repository and each method exactly once; catch throwing dependency-property access and return the fixed construction TypeError. Inspect no unrelated property/method and do not probe record existence.
construction.purity: Synchronous and I/O-free. Zero repository reads/writes, DB prepare/batch, authorization, resolver, environment, network, migration, provisioning or clock calls. No fallback repository/source and no constructor invocation.
construction.identity: Both captured functions must be invoked with the same exact supplied repository as receiver. Retain that object; do not copy/reconstruct it or create a second repository. Subsequent replacement of its method properties must not retarget captured methods. No requirement to share with an opaque existing K bundle: its repository is unavailable by design. Where a trusted future caller already owns the repository, reuse that same instance for projection and any separately constructed draft service; do not extract it from a private service or create duplicates merely for Q.

readExecution: getProduct(id, version) invokes the captured repository.getProduct.call(repository, id, version) once; getRecipe does the same for its method. Preserve all values/references exactly, including invalid/noncanonical inputs for the underlying authority to reject.

Return the exact underlying Promise unchanged; wrappers need not be async. No added await/result cloning/domain validation/envelope projection/snapshot freezing. Repository remains the raw-read/domain authority and menu consumers remain verification authority.

A synchronous dependency throw propagates unchanged; async rejection propagates unchanged, including error identity/type. Do not catch, sanitize, log or interpret read failures in Q. Q is internal and never a user feedback boundary; existing menu/service layers sanitize failures.

Valid found and not-found results remain unchanged by identity. Malformed fulfilled results from a broken/injected dependency also pass unchanged to existing menu fail-closed verification; Q must not fabricate not-found or duplicate domain validation.

No latest substitution, normalization, automatic retry, evidence retargeting, missing-reference repair, readiness interpretation, merging or mutation. Detached/frozen history is inherited from the repository; Q does not guarantee arbitrary faulty providers are domain-valid.
Concurrent reads use invocation-local arguments and return values; no request/result/auth cache or mutable global state. Q does not add an atomic product-plus-recipe snapshot guarantee.
databaseTopology: Current code permits FOOD-001 and FOOD-002 repositories to use the same injected database with separate table families, or separately selected databases through independent dependencies. FOOD-002G does not impose physical cross-database FOOD-001 foreign keys; it verifies references through injected reads. Production topology remains unresolved. Q construction/testing requires neither topology selection nor database access and establishes no cross-database consistency guarantee.
futureWiring: A separately approved trusted server composition obtains/constructs the approved FOOD-001 repository, projects createFoodMenuReadDependencies({ repository }), and supplies that result as readDependencies to createPrivateFoodMenuRuntimeComposition/createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeComposition or createPrivateFoodMenuOperationRuntimeFromServerContext. H/J/L accept it already; no interface changes or casts needed. That caller owns menu database/bindingName, session/admin configuration and source lifecycle. Q acquires none of them and does not expose the underlying repository through any runtime result.

blockerReclassification.exactReadArchitecture: After Q implementation/validation the narrow raw-read projection seam is resolved; no service-envelope adapter is needed. Existing contracts already support it statically.
blockerReclassification.exactReadProductionIntegration: Still unresolved until trusted upstream composition selects the FOOD-001 historical source, constructs or reuses its repository and supplies the projection. Q alone does not completely remove O/P's production exact-read composition blocker or make routes ready.

Separately approve binding provisioning/configuration and correct-target migrations/recovery verification
Only then authorize faithful route registration/integration verification, deployment and separate private activation
blockerReclassification.status: P HTTP composition is complete. Production route readiness remains BLOCKED. Q removes no production approval gate and does not select any binding/target/principal/origin.

tests: Synchronous frozen two-method output, zero construction reads/auth/database/network calls, no caller-owned mutation/freezing or exposed repository/database internals
Malformed/null/array/missing outer/repository input, each noncallable method and throwing input/method getters produce the exact fixed construction TypeError; only required properties inspected once

Exact product/recipe argument identity and explicit historical version reach the correct captured method exactly once with original repository receiver; method replacement does not retarget; no unrelated method invoked
Return the exact original Promise and preserve found/not-found result identity. Preserve sync throw and rejection error identity; do not convert storage/validation failures to not-found
Real in-memory FOOD-001 historical product and recipe reads preserve exact version, recorded recipe reference, detached/deeply frozen snapshots and no latest substitution after revisions

Malformed fulfilled dependency results reach real menu repository verification unchanged and become storage; missing dependency is invalid-input for new content and storage for existing stored records; thrown errors remain sanitized only by existing menu/service authorities
Two independent concurrent reads share no mutable invocation state; no authorization cache/token exists; denied menu service operations invoke the projected dependencies zero times
Static assignments to FoodMenuReadDependencies and existing H/J/L readDependencies inputs compile without consumer casts; no new parallel exact-read abstraction
No mutations/list/history/latest methods reachable from result and no runtime/D1/environment/session/HTTP/route/global/logging imports or operations; no configured DB used
futureValidation: Relevant FOOD-001 repository/domain/service and FOOD-002 menu/runtime regressions without configured DB or migration execution
Normal build without unrelated baseline fixes
